transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-21
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~47 min
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Atlas Head of ML), Daniel Kim (Atlas Infra), Sara Lopez (Atlas PM)

Summary:
- Quick review of this week's benchmark results comparing Redwood vs the BaselineCloud provider.
- Redwood shows improved p95 latency and throughput in most steady-state tests; p99 tail still close on cold starts.
- Discussed batching, KV/prefix cache, and quantization tradeoffs; agreed to run extended high-concurrency test and tune batch settings.
- Next steps: Redwood to share raw logs/spreadsheet; Atlas to run longer load test; schedule exec sync.

Topics:
1) p95/p99 latency comparison
2) throughput tokens/sec & sustained QPS
3) impact of KV cache and batching
4) quantization/quality tradeoffs and cost delta
5) next steps and pilot decision timeline

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Maya from Redwood, i'll kick us off. we ran the set of bench marks you gave us last week, um, and we put them side-by-side with the BaselineCloud numbers you provided. Liam's got the details.
[00:22] Liam: yeah hi, hi, thanks. quick note, the sheet link is in chat, Benchmark spreadsheet: https://redwood.app/sheets/atlas-poc-benchmarks. um, high-level, steady-state p95 on Redwood across the 2 models you sent was ~210ms versus BaselineCloud at ~340ms (same tokenization and prompt mix). throughput for tokens/sec was about 85 tokens/sec sustained on our "reserved" config vs 68 on baseline under identical driver load.
[00:48] Priya: okay that's promising, can you remind me what config you used for "reserved"? like gpu size and batch settings?
[00:56] Liam: sure, we used a 4xA10s equivalent pool (we annotated it as r4-a10), batching target 128ms latency bucket, max batch size 64 for model-a, and enabled prefix KV caching for repeated context. quantization was int8 for the faster runs unless we noted otherwise.
[01:20] Daniel: when you say p95 210, is that end-to-end including network hop to our region? we ran BaselineCloud from us-east-1, same as your run?
[01:29] Liam: yes we pinned to us-east-1 region, driver ran in the same AZ, and numbers are end-to-end excluding client-side application overhead; we included the small network roundtrip inside the same region.
[01:38] Sara: any p99 numbers? the product team cares about tail for interactive flows.
[01:43] Liam: p99 was 560ms on Redwood for that session, BaselineCloud was about 520ms. so p99 is comparable; we saw most of the p99 variance come from cold-worker spin-ups and occasional larger batches in the queue. our continuous batching strategy tends to improve the p95 more than the p99 until we tune worker keep-alive and warm pool sizes.
[02:07] Priya: hmm that matches our experience elsewhere. the p95 improvement is good but p99 being similar makes me worry about unpredictable tail for users. can KV cache help here?
[02:16] Liam: yes, prefix/KV cache reduced token generation time by ~25% on repeated session flows in our tests. it mostly helps the early decode steps and avoids re-computing key/value for repeated prefixes. that lowered both p95 and p99 in the subset of tests with high prefix repetition.
[02:33] Maya: also wanted to mention inference kernels - for your model variant we chose a different kernel path that favors attention optimizations; that contributes to the per-token improvement. we'll include kernel mapping in the doc.
[02:45] Daniel: did you try larger batch sizes? i'm worried about latency-sensitive paths vs batching that increases throughput.
[02:51] Liam: yes, we ran a batch sensitivity sweep—batch size 32, 64, 128—and observed that mean throughput scales until batch size ~64; beyond that the latency for single-request flows spikes. our recommended sweet spot for Atlas' interactive mix was target batch 64 with a 90ms batching window.
[03:14] Priya: what about quantization quality? we can't accept >2% drop in accuracy for our clinical summarization tasks.
[03:22] Liam: int8 gave about ~1.5% delta on our automatic evals for the summarization prompt set; int4 experiments reduced cost more but had higher quality delta (2.8-3.5%). i would recommend int8 for pilot to balance cost vs quality. we can share the eval prompts and diffs.
[03:40] Sara: did BaselineCloud run with quantization too? could that be a reason for baseline higher latency?
[03:45] Liam: BaselineCloud runs a conservative fp16 path mostly; they had fewer kernel optimizations for this model shape and their autoscaling profile appears to spin up extra workers faster which helps their p99 a bit but hurts steady throughput. so different trade-offs.
[04:03] Priya: can you expand on cost numbers? i.e., unit cost per 1M tokens after quantization and batching?
[04:10] Maya: short answer: on our dedicated config with int8 + KV + batching the estimated unit cost is roughly 40% lower than BaselineCloud for your workload mix. we'll put a per-scenario breakdown in the spreadsheet.
[04:21] Daniel: are those estimates including amortized reserved capacity? 
[04:25] Maya: yes includes reserved capacity for dedicated pools, with assumptions listed in the sheet (commit months, utilization rates). we'll mark those assumptions clearly.
[04:32] Liam: one more data point: cold-starts. BaselineCloud's quick spin-up lowered their observed p99 in short bursts because they spin up many small instances; Redwood favors slightly larger warm pools which preserves steady throughput and unit cost. we can tune for more aggressive warm scaling if you prefer tail over cost.
[04:55] Priya: okay, let's talk about the long run test you recommended — what will that look like?
[05:01] Liam: we suggest a 48-hour run with concurrency ramp to 200 concurrent sessions, token mix attached in the sheet, and intermittent burst tests to simulate peak. that will expose autoscaling behavior, tail, and sustained unit cost.
[05:15] Daniel: i can run that on our infra tomorrow, will use your driver and share logs. what's the log format?
[05:20] Liam: JSONL with per-request timing and server-side trace ids; link to driver in the spreadsheet and instructions. we'll include a quick runbook in the next email.
[05:29] Sara: any security or compliance stuff we need to confirm for the dedicated pilot? SSO, audit logs, KMS?
[05:34] Maya: yes, we have SOC2 + ISO artifacts; dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and VPC peering for Private deployments. i'll attach the full security packet and a short summary for the pilot.
[05:46] Priya: great. and will logs include per-token cost breakdown? product wants token-level cost to attribute features.
[05:52] Liam: yes, our trace includes token count and cost attribution per route; Console will show token-level breakdowns and per-model dashboards — we'll share screenshots.
[06:02] Priya: what's the expected timeline to tune and get results back?
[06:06] Maya: if you run the 48-hour test by end of week, Liam can analyze and we'll deliver a tuned config + cost delta by next Wednesday. that keeps us on track for an exec pilot decision the week of 3/30.
[06:17] Daniel: sounds reasonable. one question — our legal asked about data residency, does Redwood keep logs? are logs persisted in our tenant only?
[06:25] Maya: for Dedicated we keep logs in your tenant, with retention policies configurable; for Private we can deploy behind your VPC and logs never leave your network. we'll include the legal/security note in the packet.
[06:36] Priya: ok thanks. small nit — the p99 numbers being slightly worse sometimes, do you have a quick mitigation?
[06:42] Liam: yes increase warm pool keep-alives and reduce max batch window; that brings p99 down at the expense of some throughput/cost. we can provide a knobbed comparison (aggressive-warm vs cost-opt) in the next sheet.
[06:55] Sara: any surprises in the raw logs you want to call out?
[06:58] Liam: we observed two anomalous spikes correlated with a driver-side GC event in the test harness; not infra. we'll filter those out and re-run the 10-minute burst test.
[07:09] Priya: ok let's talk decisions — if Redwood can hit p95 <250ms and keep quality delta <2% while showing ~30% unit cost savings, that seems compelling.
[07:18] Maya: agreed, that's the informal bar we heard last week. we'll aim for that.
[07:23] Daniel: one operational ask — can we get an API key scoped to the pilot with restricted quota so we don't pollute production?
[07:29] Maya: yes we can provision pilot keys and RBAC roles; we'll include in the runbook.
[07:34] Priya: ok perfect. next steps recap?
[07:37] Maya: recap: 1) Redwood to share full benchmark spreadsheet + raw logs by 3/23; 2) Atlas (Daniel) to run 48-hour load test and share logs by 3/28; 3) Redwood (Liam) to deliver tuned batching/KV + cost estimate by 3/25; 4) Maya to send pricing/pilot SLA and security packet by 3/23; 5) schedule exec sync week of 3/30.
[07:59] Priya: good, i'll confirm success criteria and loop in security/legal as needed.
[08:05] Sara: thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[08:07] Maya: thanks all, talk soon.

End of transcript.
